figmaSource.usage: Use this file as the single source of truth for component specs, tokens, and patterns. When matching UI to Figma, reference node IDs from this file.

pageHeader.structure: Optional breadcrumbs (Level 1 > Current level, 14px medium #232a31) → Title row: page title (24px bold, 28px line-height, #232a31) left-aligned; optional primary button + icon button right-aligned with 12px gap. Optional slot below for filter chips (Sort & filter row).
pageHeader.component: PageHeader in src/components/PageHeader.tsx; used on Overview, Settings, Issues, Feed health, Issue detail, and Content performance (KPI) pages.

overview.purpose: Partner-facing analytics dashboard for monitoring KPI performance, feed health, and issue diagnostics across Yahoo surfaces.
designGoals: Enterprise-grade clarity and trustworthiness for B2B users.
Information-dense layouts that remain scannable and calm under load.
Consistent visual hierarchy across KPIs, tables, and detail views.
Responsive behavior that preserves core structure from laptop to desktop.
visualTone: Neutral, product-centric, with restrained color usage.
Functional rather than flashy; emphasis on typography and spacing.
Status color is reserved for semantic meaning (success, warning, error).

layout.pageMaxWidth: Approx. 1100–1200px content width centered in the viewport.
layout.outerPadding: Horizontal padding of 16–24px on small screens, 24–32px on large screens.
layout.verticalRhythm: Vertical spacing in 16–24px increments between major sections.
layout.gridUsage: 2–4 column responsive grids for KPIs; 2-column master-detail layouts on larger screens.

typography.baseFont: System or UDS default sans-serif; Phase 2 should align with Figma’s chosen Yahoo typefaces.

sizes.body: Approx. 13–14px regular for body copy and table content.
sizes.caption: Approx. 11–12px for helper text, metadata, and labels.

hierarchy: Use uppercase micro-labels (very small size, increased letter-spacing) above key headings for context.
Use semibold weight and darker color for primary titles and numeric KPIs.
Use lighter, desaturated text for secondary descriptions and timestamps.

background.app: Soft neutral gray background behind content areas.
background.surface: White or near-white cards for primary content blocks.

text.primary: Dark neutral slate for titles and important values.
text.secondary: Mid-tone neutral slate for secondary info and labels.
text.muted: Lighter neutral slate for metadata and helper text.

status.success: Emerald/green family for healthy states and improving trends.
status.warning: Amber/orange family for degraded but not critical states.
status.error: Rose/red family for failures, high error rates, and critical issues.
status.neutral: Slate/gray for inactive or baseline states.

surfaceAndElevation.cards: Rounded rectangles with light borders and subtle shadows to separate from the background.
surfaceAndElevation.tables: Flat white surfaces with header underlines and row dividers instead of heavy borders.
surfaceAndElevation.emphasis: Use border + background contrast first; only add stronger shadows for highly prominent panels.

interaction.hitTargets: Minimum tap/click target of ~32px height for interactive elements.
interaction.hoverStates: Subtle background or border changes, avoiding large jumps in color saturation.
interaction.focusStates: Clearly visible outlines in Phase 2; align with UDS focus-ring tokens.

AppShell.role: Top-level chrome that frames all analytics content: side navigation, global header, and page content area.
structure: Left-aligned vertical sidebar approximately 252px wide, spanning full viewport height.
Global header strip 64px tall at the top of the main content column, aligned with the Figma shell.
Main content area below the header with comfortable horizontal padding and scrollable body.
visualGuidelines: Sidebar is a white surface with a subtle right keyline, 252px wide; nav rows are 14px type with left icons and an active-state indicator line.

Global header is a white 64px bar with a subtle bottom keyline; left lockup contains a purple circular icon button and the Yahoo Partner Portal wordmark in dark text. Right side contains a purple circular search button and a gray profile button that opens a dropdown menu.
Main content background remains light neutral; cards and tables sit on white surfaces within this frame.
Navigation labels in the sidebar should map closely to the Figma structure, even when some entries are non-functional in the prototype.

KpiCard.role: Chip-style tile summarizing a single KPI with a primary value and directional change context. Two-tier layout on Overview: Primary (large) and Secondary (small) chips.
structure: Top row: small, uppercase KPI label on the left; optional delta badge on the right.
Middle row: large (primary) or medium (secondary) numeric value, optionally with unit suffix (%, $, etc.).
Bottom row: one-line helper text summarizing the trend or driver.

variants.primary: Larger chip: heading row (label + info icon), second row (value + delta pill + sparkline). Sparkline is ECharts line chart, 271×60px, no axes/labels, dark line, small circle points. Used for the top row of two on Overview.
variants.secondary: Smaller chip: tighter padding, smaller value (e.g. text-xl), used in the 3+3 grid below. No chart.

visualGuidelines: Card corners are rounded with a light border and soft shadow to feel clickable but not heavy.
Primary value should be the largest text in the tile; label and helper text are clearly subordinate.
Delta badge uses color-coded background and text to indicate positive vs. negative vs. neutral movement.
Trend iconography (chevrons, arrows) is small and secondary to the numeric delta.

DashboardOverview.role: Landing view for the portal, combining KPI snapshots (two-tier chip grid) with content performance tables that support scanning and comparison.
layout: Top: two large Primary KPI chips in a single row (e.g. Total impressions, Estimated revenue).
Below: six smaller Secondary KPI chips in a 3-column grid (e.g. CTR, Feed error rate, Active feeds, Fill rate, Avg. position, Content items).
Below: a two-column section pairing a performance panel with a ranked content table (Rank / Title / Views).
Below: a full-width brand comparison table with inline bar visualization and multiple metrics per brand.
Sections separated with comfortable vertical space but visually unified via consistent card styling.
visualGuidelines: Keep KPI tiles tightly aligned in a grid to enable quick side-by-side comparison.
Tables are flat white surfaces with thin header rules and row dividers; avoid zebra-striping.
Use underlined text links for content titles and brand names; truncate long text with ellipsis.

RankedContentTable.role: Compact ranked list of top content items for the selected time window, optimized for quick scanning.
visualGuidelines: 3-column table: Rank (49px), Title (flex), Views (80px).
Header row is 33px tall with 14px medium labels; body rows are ~55.8px tall with thin dividers.
Titles are underlined links in a secondary text color and truncate to one line with ellipsis.
Numbers are tabular and aligned consistently; keep the table surface flat and clean.

BrandComparisonTable.role: Side-by-side comparison of top brands, combining numeric metrics with an inline bar to communicate magnitude at a glance.
visualGuidelines: Header row is 52px tall; include an 8px spacer row before the data for visual breathing room.
Data rows are 46px tall with thin row dividers; no zebra-striping.
Views column includes an inline bar (16px tall) in purple (#6866e9) with asymmetric rounding (2px left, 12px right) plus the formatted number.
Brand names are underlined; use truncation to keep column widths stable.

FilterChipRow.role: Compact filter controls shown beneath the page header, allowing quick narrowing of the overview dataset.
visualGuidelines: Six pill-shaped chips in a single row with 16px gaps (wrap on smaller screens).
Chip height is 36px (px=16, py=8) with full rounding.
Applied chip uses a light blue-gray fill (#f5f8fa) with a 1px dark border (#232a31) and a trailing X icon.
Dropdown chips use white fill with a 1px muted border (#e0e4e9) and a trailing chevron-down icon.
Typography is 14px medium with 20px line height, using product sans styling and primary text color (#232a31).
Dropdown menus are 240px wide, white surface, 8px radius, subtle shadow; multi-select toggles auto-apply on click (no Apply step).
Date filter presets auto-apply and close; Custom opens a date-range + time + timezone view with Save/Clear (single time applies to both start & end).

KpiDrilldownPage.role: Detail view for a single KPI, showing how it evolves over time and summarizing performance.
layout: Intro header with micro-label, KPI title, and a short descriptive sentence.
Main content: left side reserved for a timeseries chart; right side for metric summary and perhaps filters in Phase 2.
Chart area framed as a card with clear axes and gridlines in Phase 2, currently a placeholder panel.
visualGuidelines: Keep chart area visually dominant but not overwhelming; surrounding whitespace is important.
Summary card should read like an executive snapshot: current value, delta, and a brief interpretation.
If filters or time range selectors are added later, align them with UDS button and chip patterns.

ContentPerformancePage.role: Metric-focused content performance screen with filter chips, a full-width line chart, and a tabbed table that switches metrics.
layout: Page header includes section label + 24px title and a right-side download icon.
Below the title, a row of filter chips (Last 7 days applied + multiple dropdown chips).
Full-width line chart card with visible axes and light gridlines.
Tabbed table section with 6 metric tabs and summary KPI tiles above the table.
visualGuidelines: Tabs use 14px medium labels; the active tab has a 4px accent underline (#7d2eff).
Summary tiles are 10px radius, 24px padding, light border (#f0f3f5), with 24px bold values in purple (#7c49fc).
Table rows are 52px tall with thin dividers (#f0f3f5) and 14px table text.

FeedHealthView.role: Operational dashboard for feed ingestion status and error hotspots.
layout: Header summarizing the number of configured feeds and overall health.
Single wide table listing feeds with columns for name, vertical, status, error rate, open issues, and last ingested.
Table designed for quick scanning left-to-right, with key status and numerical columns right-aligned as appropriate.
visualGuidelines: Status column uses labeled pills with semantic colors and small dot indicators.
Error rate and open issue counts should be align-right to simplify scanning of magnitudes.
Last ingested timestamps should use a lighter text color and smaller size to read as metadata.

IssuesList.role: Queue of active feed issues that need investigation or action.
layout: Table with columns for issue title/code, feed name, severity, affected items, and last seen timestamp.
Issue titles behave as links to the issue detail page.
Severity is represented as a pill with suitable color intensity corresponding to impact.
visualGuidelines: Issue titles should be easy to scan; codes can be shown as small uppercase metadata underneath.
Severity colors must be distinct from generic status colors but still within the overall palette.
Affected items counts are formatted with thousand separators to reinforce scale.

IssueDetailPage.role: Deep dive into a single issue with full technical context and recommended actions.
layout: Header with micro-label, issue title, and a compact line showing feed and code.
Two-column body: primary technical details on the left; summary stats and recommended actions stacked on the right.
Cards aligned vertically with consistent padding and spacing to feel like a coherent detail view.
visualGuidelines: Technical details may include preformatted or multi-paragraph text; use readable line length and spacing.
Summary card emphasizes critical numbers (severity, affected items) with clear labels and right alignment.
Recommended actions appear as an ordered list for easy step-by-step execution.

udsIntegration: Continue using the UDS Tailwind plugin as the basis for typography, spacing, and radii tokens.
Layer UDS React components (Badge, Chip, IconButton, Menu, Toast, Tooltip, Input) gradually to replace custom primitives where they map cleanly to the Figma design.
Align global providers such as UDSConfigProvider, UDSBreakpointsConfigProvider, and UDSToastConfigProvider with the final design tokens.
visualRefinements: Replace generic colors with the exact Yahoo palette and semantic tokens from Figma.
Adjust typography to match the precise Figma ramp (font families, font weights, line heights).
Refine spacing and corner radii across cards and tables to match the original Yahoo Partner Portal spec.
Introduce iconography from UDS Icons for navigation, severity indicators, and contextual actions.
consistencyPrinciples: Every interactive element should map to a known component pattern (button, chip, link, menu item, etc.).
Avoid one-off styles; prefer reusable classes or UDS components to encourage consistency across screens.
When in doubt, align with UDS defaults first, then override minimally to match the Figma source.
All Figma references (component specs, tokens, patterns) must come from the Platforms Design System file (see figmaSource). Share specific node IDs from that file when requesting visual updates.
